solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like a failing old tavern, stuck with rum nosh, rotten

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed and fallen apart, so the preceding letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written; 'with' is part of the run of words but adds no letters beyond those of stuck, rum and nosh

explanation.surface: A grim pub where the food is so bad that the rum and grub have gone off together.
explanation.walkthrough: Only STUCK, RUM and NOSH are shuffled; 'with' just joins them. Nosh is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom-shrunk is Chambers' word for having lost customers, the fate of a failing inn or shop.

clue.text: Holding power, truncheon accompanies work — here?

definitions.text: Holding power, truncheon accompanies work — here?

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
a cosh is a short heavy club, like a policeman's truncheon
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A police station is where those with power and truncheons go about their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accompanies' just puts the work after the truncheon. Read whole, the clue with its 'here?' describes the place, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cop shop is informal slang for a police station, where officers armed with truncheons do their duty.

clue.text: Arrive gracefully, as young suitor about noon (6, two words)

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is placed round the second

blocks.note: a swain is a young lover or wooer
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A young admirer turns up at midday with elegant composure.
explanation.definitionFit: To swan in is the idiom for entering in an elegant, unconcerned and showy manner.

clue.text: Restart mine worked out? One washes ore from deposits

indicators.note: something worked out has been reprocessed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Should an exhausted mine be reopened? Someone sluicing ore from the deposits might think so.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin-streamer is a worker who recovers tin ore by washing it out of alluvial deposits, especially in Cornwall.

clue.text: Male on track having turned up for colourful birds

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
spore is an old variant of spoor, an animal's track, found in the OED

explanation.surface: A man at the racecourse is spotted bird-watching.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers spells the track word SPOOR; SPORE is the older variant. 'on' simply places the male above it in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Merops is the genus of the bee-eaters, brightly plumaged birds of warm countries.

clue.text: Part of tack which a merchantman has on board

indicators.note: a ship with something on board carries it inside, so the letters sit within the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of which, the a, and the start of merchantman

explanation.surface: A merchant ship carries some harness among its cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Tack is a horse's harness and saddlery, and a hame is one of the curved bars of a draught horse's collar.

clue.text: Lift: Mary missing first in use

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the named portion is taken away from the longer word
in places the trimmed word inside the other one

blocks.note: primary means first in order
taken as written, the letters to remove
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction on a hoist about letting Mary go first.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Mary the one missing; in fact the word for 'first' is the one that loses her, and what remains goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprise means to rise up or a rising, and Chambers allows it as lift or ascent.

clue.text: Pest lives in shade

indicators.note: in puts the first word inside the second

blocks.note: is means exists or lives
a nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or colour

explanation.surface: A garden pest lurks in the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is a person or thing that annoys, which is exactly a nuisance.

clue.text: Odist a Sekt befuddled

indicators.note: befuddled means muddled by drink, so the letters are confused into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; Sekt is German sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A poet who has had a glass of German fizz too many.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the wine to work making the poet tipsy; it is the letters that are befuddled.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats wrote the great odes, to a Nightingale and on a Grecian Urn among them, so he is the odist par excellence.

clue.text: Organized ladies diving into Scottish river, rarely drunk on malt

indicators.note: diving into a river puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: WI is the Women's Institute, an organisation of women in Britain
the Spey is a river in the Scottish Highlands, famous for whisky

explanation.surface: Members of a women's club go swimming in a Highland river famous for its distilleries.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spey valley is whisky country, which suits the surface, but the malt here is malt liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Swipes is thin poor beer brewed from malt, and Chambers marks swipey, tipsy from it, as rare.

clue.text: What's said to guy inverting half of ring-bark?

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is a single letter, here the front one
inverting turns the down light upside down, so the pieces are read in the opposite order

blocks.note: the first half of the little word of
a ring is round like the letter O
to bay is to bark like a hound

explanation.surface: A tree-surgery question: what do you call it when you strip a ring of bark?
explanation.walkthrough: Ring-bark looks like one word (to strip a band of bark from a tree) but splits into two pieces. To guy is to mock or jeer at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaboo, or yah-boo, is an exclamation of derision, the sort of jeer flung at someone you are mocking.

clue.text: Bert and Elsie I see irregularly used as names

indicators.note: used irregularly means put in no fixed order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the letter C is pronounced like the word see

explanation.surface: Someone notices that ordinary Bert and Elsie are being treated as though they were famous names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' merely joins the two first names; the C comes from the sound of 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is a famous person, and big names is the everyday phrase for famous people.

clue.text: Draught of sole abandoned by tar?

indicators.note: a word abandoned by some letters has been left without them, so they are removed

blocks.note: plantar means relating to the sole of the foot
taken as written, the letters to drop

explanation.surface: A seafaring question about a sailor's sole meal or a ship's draught.
explanation.walkthrough: Draught tempts toward beer or a ship's depth, and tar toward a sailor; draught here is the drawing sense, as in draft.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught, in the sense of a preliminary drawing or sketch, is a plan.

clue.text: Astringent I earmark for treatment

indicators.note: something given treatment is processed and worked over, so its letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor sets aside an astringent medicine for a patient's treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Krameria, or rhatany, is a South American shrub whose root yields an astringent drug.

clue.text: Seconds ahead, being once past

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds
puts the seconds in front
ens is the philosophical term for being or existence

explanation.surface: A runner seconds in front, but now beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a link word but supplies the second piece, the philosopher's word for existence. 'Once' marks the definition as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Sens is an obsolete form of since, meaning ago or in the past, as in 'long sens'.

clue.text: New column, curtailed with time, for laureate

indicators.note: curtailed means having had its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an obelisk is a tall tapering stone column
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A newspaper's new column is cut short to make room for news of a prizewinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Column suggests a newspaper feature, but it is the stone pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nobelist is a winner of a Nobel prize, and a laureate is an honoured prizewinner.

clue.text: Oath from Jock: 'It's a wee bittie hard'

blocks.note: hait, or haet, is Scots for a whit or the smallest amount
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Scotsman swears mildly and complains that something is a little bit difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is the stock nickname for a Scotsman, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Haith is a Scots exclamation, a mild oath roughly meaning 'faith!'

clue.text: A short book on Eton taken out when one pleases (8, two words)

indicators.note: taken out suggests dismantled or disordered, so the school's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
vol is the short form of volume, a book
taken as written
the Eton letters left once on is used

explanation.surface: A pupil borrows a book about Eton and takes it out whenever they like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the rest after the book; the jumbled school supplies the tail. Eton is the famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A volonté is a French phrase, used in English, meaning at will or whenever one likes.

clue.text: Maine's crack troops? They're flat-topped

blocks.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
the SAS is the Special Air Service, Britain's elite special forces regiment

explanation.surface: A question about whether the troops from Maine are the elite ones, with a flat-topped haircut joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests soldiers' crew cuts, but the flat tops are geological.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesas are steep-sided hills with level summits, so they are flat-topped landforms.

clue.text: Ebbing river abroad cracks stern badly, soaking back

indicators.note: an ebbing tide flows back, so the river's name runs backwards
badly means done wrong, so the letters are put in the wrong order
something that cracks a thing breaks into it and ends up inside

blocks.note: taken as written
the Ebro is a river in Spain

explanation.surface: A boat is damaged at the stern as a foreign river's current recedes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebbing sounds like the tide, which fits the boat, but it turns the river round.
explanation.definitionFit: Resorbent means reabsorbing, taking in again what was given out, so soaking back up.

clue.text: Am avoiding dynamiter at large with a short fuse!

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping out of, so those letters are taken out of the longer word
at large means roaming free, so the remaining letters are let loose in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeping clear of a bomber on the loose, whose bomb has a short fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: Short fuse looks like part of the bomb, but it is the idiom for a quick temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tindery means like tinder, readily set alight, and so figuratively irascible or quick to flare up.

clue.text: Reader having to admit old wife is computer whizz (9, two words)

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the extra letters go inside

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
W is the abbreviation for wife
a peruser is someone who reads carefully

explanation.surface: A reader has to confess that his elderly wife is a whizz with computers.
explanation.definitionFit: A power user is someone who uses a computer's advanced features expertly, an IT whizz.

clue.text: Right in centre of parade, on the rise — value doubled (at least)

indicators.note: in a down entry, on the rise means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
in the centre of places one piece in the middle of the other

blocks.note: to parade is to show off, and a parade is a show
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Things look right in the middle of a rising parade, and the value of something doubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Value doubled (at least)' means value in the plural, two or more of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth is value, and making it plural, two or more values, gives worths.

clue.text: Like water vessel number dipped in river

indicators.note: something dipped in is put inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: the Ural is a river of Russia and Kazakhstan
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A numbered jug is dipped into a river to fill it.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vessel, and urnal is the adjective meaning of or like an urn.

clue.text: Confederate solicitor receiving cheers

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: SL is the abbreviation for solicitor
ta-ta is an informal goodbye, as cheers can be

explanation.surface: A conspirator's lawyer accepts a farewell toast.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain cheers is a casual goodbye as well as a toast or thanks, which is the sense needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Statal means relating to a state, especially a state within a federation, so confederate in that sense.

clue.text: Membranous coverings displaying limitless allure?

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundary letters, so the first and last go

blocks.note: allure is sexual attractiveness

explanation.surface: Sheer fabrics that reveal boundless sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests revealing clothing; the coverings are microscopic.
explanation.definitionFit: The exine is the tough outer layer of a pollen grain or spore wall, a membranous coat.

clue.text: Squelch round the highlands? It's stag's head, look, one's after

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the front letter of stag
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A deer-stalker in the Highlands sees a stag's head and squelches through the bog after it.
explanation.walkthrough: Squelch suggests boggy ground, but it is the noun for a crushing retort; 'round the highlands' marks the word as Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloan is Scots for a snub or rebuke, and a squelch is a crushing put-down.

clue.text: Herd youngster? This horn'd guy possibly

definitions.text: Herd youngster? This horn'd guy possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be rearranged
the clue says the pool equals this answer plus the other phrase, so that phrase must be taken out

blocks.note: taken as written, the full letter pool
taken as written, the letters to remove from the pool

explanation.surface: Is the young beast in the herd this horned fellow?
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer together with HORN'D GUY is an anagram of HERD YOUNGSTER. The clue also defines it repeatedly: to herd is to steer, and a steer is a young horned ox.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a young castrated ox, horned; and to steer is to guide, as one herds cattle or guys with a rope.

clue.text: Cock, maybe, cross in appearance

indicators.note: in puts the first item inside the second

blocks.note: mien is a person's look or bearing
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A rooster looks angry.
explanation.walkthrough: Cock suggests a rooster and cross an angry look; a cock is also a small conical heap, as in haycock.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixen is a dunghill, and a cock is a heap, so a mixen is one example of a cock.

clue.text: Not accepted in Sicilian town, left describing stomach pains

indicators.note: something not accepted in a place is shut out of it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for accepted
Taormina is a hilltop resort town in Sicily
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A tourist turned away from a Sicilian resort, left with an upset stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormina are acute colicky gripes in the bowels, and torminal is the adjective for such pains.

clue.text: Part of the eye mostly recalling smiling ones?

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: from the song When Irish Eyes Are Smiling, where the smiling eyes are Irish ones

explanation.surface: A wistful look at the eye, recalling a sentimental song about smiling eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the song reference: the smiling ones are Irish eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is the coloured ring of muscle around the pupil of the eye.

clue.text: Kindle, obsolete, leads to this in next decade

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned e-reader, a Kindle, made obsolete by what comes in the next ten years.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindle looks like the Amazon e-reader; it is the verb to set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tind is an obsolete verb meaning to kindle or set on fire, related to tinder.

clue.text: With a passage for food to join, took dinner?

blocks.note: to enter a club is to join it
to eat is to take a meal

explanation.surface: Someone joins a dining club and asks whether they ate there.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterate describes an animal having an alimentary canal, a distinct gut through which food passes.

clue.text: Intrinsically anxious, lacking cure (4, two words)

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the named letters are taken away

blocks.note: insecure means anxious or lacking confidence
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A patient is anxious by nature, with no remedy to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In se is a Latin phrase meaning in itself, which is what intrinsically means.

clue.text: At sea head, ay, do so to windward as before

definitions.text: do so to windward as before

blocks.note: surface padding that sets the nautical scene and points to the ship's sense of head
the head is a ship's toilet, and lav is short for lavatory
ay means always, as does e'er, the poetic form of ever

explanation.surface: A sailor's instruction at sea: head off, aye aye, and do it into the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' sets the scene and signals the nautical head, a ship's toilet. Ay here is the old word for always, not yes; 'do so' means tack, as in sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Laveer is an old word meaning to beat or tack to windward, zigzagging into the wind.

clue.text: 'E's caught by S. Liston's cut, on going inside count — as invincibility progresses?

indicators.note: going means departing, so that small word leaves the boxer's name
cut as cards are cut and mixed, so the letters are reordered
caught by brings the two groups of letters together into one pool
inside places the jumble within the other word

blocks.note: to count on someone is to rely on them
taken as written, the letters of he's with the h dropped
taken as written; Sonny Liston was a world heavyweight boxing champion

explanation.surface: A boxing commentary: he's caught by Liston's cut, the count goes on, and the champion looks unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word sounds like a boxing report. 'On going' removes the little word from Liston's name before the jumble goes inside the word for count.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistlessly means irresistibly, in a way that cannot be withstood, as an invincible fighter advances.
